request.spec: The request may set boolean 'sharesHousehold'. When true, allow an owner at an address already used by a same-lastName owner, and assign both the same 'householdId' (a stable shared identifier). Return 'householdId'.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

The request may set boolean 'sharesHousehold'. When true, allow an owner at an address already used by a same-lastName owner, and assign both the same 'householdId' (a stable shared identifier). Return 'householdId'.

agent.result_text:
Green. Here's how I addressed the review:

**Finding 1 (Validate step mutating + persisting) — agreed, fixed.** `ValidateUniqueHousehold` is now a pure read-only gate: it detects the household, decides allow/reject (409), and publishes the `Household.Id`. It writes nothing and no longer carries `govern: [ transaction ]`. The back-fill (mutate existing members + save) moved into a new dedicated step, `ApplySharedHousehold`, wired after the gate and before `build`, which is the step that now carries `govern: [ transaction ]`. Governance sits on the write step, not the gate.

**Finding 2 (assignment split awkwardly) — agreed, consolidated.** The "every member gets this id" concern is now coherent: existing members are stamped in one place (`ApplySharedHousehold`), the new entity is stamped in `BuildOwner` (the split the review endorsed), and both — plus the gate — derive the match and the id from a single `Household` helper rather than reimplementing it. There's exactly one definition of membership (`Household.membersOf`) and one of the identifier (`Household.idFor`).

**Finding 3 (name no longer fits) — resolved by finding 1.** With the write responsibility moved out, `ValidateUniqueHousehold` is once again just a validation gate, so the `Validate…` prefix is accurate. The forming/assigning lives in `ApplySharedHousehold`.

**Minor (SHA-256 helper buried in the validator) — addressed.** The id-derivation and normalization now live in the small `Household` helper alongside the membership rule, so the gate is no longer accumulating generic utilities; the `Household.Id` carrier type moved there too (out of being nested in the validator).

One deliberate judgement call: `ApplySharedHousehold` both mutates and saves the existing members in a single step rather than splitting into separate `Apply` + `Save` units. The review explicitly offered `ApplySharedHousehold` / `SaveHousehold` as alternatives, and a per-member back-fill over a queried collection reads as one cohesive write; splitting it would pass a `List<Owner>` between steps for no real gain. The core concern — the write out of the gate, governance on the write step — is satisfied.

Acceptance behaviour is unchanged: owner `a` created plain, `b` joins (back-fills `a`, both get id `H`), `c` joins (finds `a`/`b` at `H`, gets `H`); `b` and `c` return the same non-blank `householdId`. Full suite: `BUILD SUCCESS`, 1 run / 0 failures.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The schema/model/openapi/DTO plumbing is all fine and idiomatically placed. The problem is concentrated in `ValidateUniqueHousehold`, which has outgrown its role.

**1. A `Validate` step is now mutating and persisting — it has become a catch-all.**
This project's naming convention (AGENTS.md) deliberately separates `Validate<E>` (bind/validate, "publishes nothing; a validation gate that only escalates") from `Apply<E>` (mutate) and `Save<E>` (persist). The rewritten `service` now does all three: it validates (409), *mutates* existing owners (`member.setHouseholdId(...)`), and *saves* them (`ownerRepository.save(member)`). The tell is that the YAML had to add `govern: [ transaction ]` to a validation step — governance leaking onto a gate is the signal that a write responsibility landed in the wrong unit. A maintainer scanning the pipeline would not expect `uniqueHousehold` to write to the database.

Suggested shape: keep `ValidateUniqueHousehold` a pure read-only gate that detects the conflict, decides allow/reject, and publishes the `HouseholdId`. Move the back-fill (mutate existing members + save) into its own step — e.g. `ApplySharedHousehold` / `SaveHousehold` with `govern: [ transaction ]` — wired after the gate. That restores the Validate/Apply/Save separation the rest of the codebase follows.

**2. The "assign the shared id" concern is split awkwardly across classes.**
The new owner is stamped in `BuildOwner` (via the `HouseholdId` variable), while existing members are stamped+saved inside `ValidateUniqueHousehold`. The same logical operation ("every member of this household gets this id") is implemented in two different units, in two different ways. Consolidating the member-stamping into one Apply/Save step (per finding 1) and letting Build stamp the new entity keeps each half coherent, but ideally the stamping logic reads as one concern rather than being half-hidden in a validator.

**3. The class name no longer describes what it does.**
`ValidateUniqueHousehold` now also *forms/assigns* households and generates stable identifiers. Even if you keep some of this co-located, the `Validate…` prefix is now a misnomer for a step that creates household membership. If the write responsibility moves out (finding 1), the name fits again.

Minor: the SHA-256 `householdId(...)` helper is a generic identifier-derivation utility embedded in the validator; co-location is defensible since it's household-specific, but it reinforces how much this one class has accumulated. Not blocking on its own.
